The solid line and black dots on the figure indicate actual existing frequencies; on the left side there is an actual black dot at 46°34′, corresponding to a relatively low noon solar altitude; at 86°34′ an actual black dot can be seen falling at the position of vertical coordinate 3. Then reason: at a certain place in the Northern Hemisphere, the lowest noon solar altitude in a year occurs on the winter solstice. From the figure, the lowest actual noon solar altitude is 46°34′, so there is 46°34′=90°-φ-23°26′, solving gives φ=20°N. The noon solar altitude on the summer solstice is 90°-|20°-23°26′|=86°34′. Returning to the figure to read the actual black dot at horizontal coordinate 86°34′, its vertical coordinate is 3, so the annual occurrence frequency of this value is 3 times.
